findings.title: Wrong metrics recorder in Mode3.Create error path
findings.body: When Storage.Create fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). The error came from d.Storage.Create and the start time (startStorage) belongs to that Storage call, so the duration should be reported as a storage metric via d.recordStorageDuration(...). As written, observability for storage errors is mis-labeled as legacy errors, and the duration bucket is attributed to the wrong store; dashboards and alerts built on these Prometheus labels will be wrong.

findings.title: Mode3.Delete puts base logger (d.Log) in ctx instead of enriched log
findings.body: The Delete method does log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method) but then ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log). All other methods (Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection) put the enriched logger (log) into the context, but Delete discards the method/kind/name values. Downstream code that calls klog.FromContext(ctx) inside Storage.Delete will lose those structured fields, breaking log correlation and metric labels that depend on context-derived values.

findings.title: Mode3.Delete success records 'name' as the kind metric label
findings.body: After a successful Storage.Delete, the code records d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Every other storage metric in this file uses options.Kind as the 'kind' label; using 'name' here produces a metric label whose values are object names rather than Kind strings (e.g. kind="my-playlist-uid"). This breaks the cardinality and semantics of the dualwriter_*_duration metrics; dashboards filtering by kind=Playlist will miss this data.

findings.title: Wrong metrics recorder in Mode3.Update error path
findings.body: Same defect as in Create: when d.Storage.Update fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). Since the error is from Storage.Update and the start time is the storage call's start, the call should be d.recordStorageDuration. As written, storage update failures are counted under legacy metrics, and the recorded duration is attributed to the wrong backend.

findings.title: Mode3.DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records storage metric
findings.body: Inside the async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine, after d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...) returns, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). The error and duration belong to the Legacy backend, so this should be d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Result: legacy DeleteCollection failures and latencies are silently counted against the storage backend, distorting dualwriter dashboards.

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from request ctx and are cancelled with it
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection the async legacy goroutines do context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...), deriving the legacy write's context from the incoming request context. As soon as the HTTP/RPC client disconnects (or the apiserver request finishes and cancels the request ctx), the derived context is cancelled and the legacy write aborts. The whole point of mode 3 ('write to legacy just as a safe measure') is to make legacy eventually consistent regardless of client behaviour, so legacy goroutines should detach from the request context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) in Go 1.21+) and only be bounded by the 10s timeout.

findings.title: Mode3 unit tests do not verify that the legacy write actually happened
findings.body: Mode3 is defined by the property that writes succeed on Storage and are then dispatched to Legacy asynchronously. In TestMode3_Create and TestMode3_Update the legacy mocks are registered, but the test returns immediately after the synchronous call without synchronising with the goroutine and never asserts that Legacy.Create/Legacy.Update was actually invoked (e.g. m.AssertCalled or a sync.WaitGroup/channel). The tests will pass even if the async legacy write is silently dropped, so they don't actually exercise the mode 3 contract. (TestMode3_Delete/DeleteCollection also lack any legacy assertion and only set up storage expectations.)

findings.title: Doc comments for Mode3 misrepresent the write order
findings.body: The doc on newDualWriterMode3 says 'Mode 3 represents writing to LegacyStorage and Storage and reading from Storage', and Create's comment says 'writes to LegacyStorage and Storage'. The implementation actually writes to Storage synchronously first and only then to LegacyStorage asynchronously; the comments imply a symmetric/ordered pair and don't mention that legacy is best-effort and async. This is the same issue as in the original code, but the PR was an opportunity to correct it.

findings.title: TestMode3_Create 'unified store fails' sets up legacy mock instead of storage mock
findings.body: The case 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' populates setupLegacyFn but leaves setupStorageFn nil. Because the test mocks share a single *mock.Mock across legacyStoreMock and storageMock, the storage call coincidentally matches the legacy expectation and the test still passes, but the intent (Storage.Create fails) and the setup (legacy mock) disagree. The test would be clearer and resilient to future refactors if the failing expectation were registered via setupStorageFn.
